newsitem.title: LEBANON: Israeli planes strike in south Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Israeli planes strike in south Lebanon.

text.p: Israeli warplanes rocketed suspected guerrilla targets in south Lebanon three times early on Wednesday, Lebanese security sources said.

They said the planes fired several rockets in three bombing runs into Iqlim al-Toufah ridge which is controlled by pro-Iranian Hizbollah (Party of God) guerrillas north of Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
In Beirut, a Hizbollah spokesman told Reuters the Israeli raids targeted areas around the villages of Louwaizeh and Iqmata in Iqlim al-Toufah since 6:30 a.m. (0430 GMT).

There was no immediate word on casualties in the air raid, the first into Lebanon since Sunday, when Israeli aircraft struck at Hizbollah targets in southeast Lebanon after a clash between Israeli troops and Moslem guerrillas.

Wednesday's air attack came a day after a five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire understanding in Lebanon said at least one Katyusha rocket was fired from south Lebanon into Israel on Friday night but it did not reprimand Lebanon.
The Katyusha was the first fired at northern Israel since the ceasefire ended a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon in April that killed some 200 people, mostly civilians.
Hizbollah, which fired volleys of Katyushas at Israel before the ceasefire, has denied responsibility for the firing of the rockets.
